title: Structure and Magnetic Properties of a Series of Heptanuclear Ln3Mn4 Molecular Clusters Constructed with Phenyl-salicylaldoxime: Observation of a Significant Magnetocaloric Effect in Gd3Mn4

material_class.structural_family: isostructural C3-symmetric Janus Ln3Mn4 oxime cluster

synthesis.procedure: Shared one-pot procedure for the isostructural series: equimolar PhSaoH2 (phenyl-salicylaldoxime), Ln(OAc)3·6H2O (Ln = Gd for 1Gd), and Mn(OAc)2·4H2O were dissolved in 20 mL of methanol, two equivalents of NEt3 were added, and the mixture was stirred for 7 h. The solution was filtered and the filtrate was left at room temperature for slow evaporation. Black block-shaped crystals formed after 3 days. The reported composition is Ln3Mn4(O)3(L)3(OAc)6(MeO)4(MeOH)3·MeOH (L = phenyl-salicylaldoxime); the CCDC formula corresponds to C58H69Gd3Mn4N3O28·3(CH3OH).
synthesis.temperature: room temperature for slow evaporation; stirring temperature not stated
synthesis.vessel_or_method: one-pot solution synthesis, filtration, and slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered; filtrate left for slow evaporation to give black block crystals

properties.summary: Static SQUID magnetism shows dominant ferromagnetic interactions: χmT rises on cooling from 300 K. At 2 K and 50 kOe the magnetization is 33.04 Nβ, near the 36.0 Nβ expectation for parallel alignment of three Gd(III), three high-spin Mn(III), and one high-spin Mn(IV). A significant magnetocaloric effect is reported, with maximum −ΔSm = 20.99 J kg−1 K−1 at 50 kOe and 6.0 K (41.55% of the calculated 50.51 J kg−1 K−1 / 103.51 J mol−1 K−1 limit), supporting magnetic-refrigeration interest. Ln–Ln exchange after subtracting the Mn4 contribution is described as weak; numerical J values for 1Gd are only in Table S2.

properties.summary: Diamagnetic Y(III) isolates the Mn(IV)Mn(III)3 unit. χmT decreases slowly on cooling, consistent with net antiferromagnetic Mn–Mn coupling and a negative Weiss constant (value not given). PHI fit of eq 1 gives J1 = −0.482 cm−1 (Mn1–Mn1), J2 = 0.230 cm−1 (Mn1–Mn2), and zJ = −0.008 cm−1. Magnetization at 2 K reaches 12.36 Nβ at 50 kOe and tends to saturate above 10 kOe, below the 15 Nβ fully ferromagnetic expectation.
